s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower limb mass with pain, swelling, and ulceration
salient_findings: Firm mass over the distal tibia extending into the calf
Anterior discharging ulcer with areas of necrosis
Reduced knee range of motion and tenderness over the left knee and proximal tibia
key_facts: 1-year history of gradually progressive pain and swelling below the left knee
Anterior discharging ulcer 12 cm in diameter
Knee range of motion was reduced
Tenderness over the left knee and proximal tibia
Laboratory studies, including complete blood count and metabolic panel, were within normal limits
Plain radiographs of the left leg demonstrated a large metadiaphyseal lesion of the tibia with soft-tissue opacity, bone erosion and destruction of the tibia and adjacent fibula

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large metadiaphyseal lesion of the tibia with soft-tissue opacity, bone erosion and destruction of the tibia and adjacent fibula

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and radiographic appearance of a large mass with ulceration and bone destruction

shortlist.label: Ewing's Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive pain and swelling with a large mass and systemic symptoms like intermittent fevers

shortlist.label: Soft Tissue Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large firm mass with ulceration and yellow discharge, suggesting soft tissue involvement

shortlist.label: Dedifferentiated Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large mass with bone destruction and soft tissue opacity, which could indicate dedifferentiation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large metadiaphyseal lesion of the tibia, bone erosion, and destruction, along with a firm mass and ulceration, is more typical of osteosarcoma, which is known for its aggressive bone destruction and soft tissue involvement.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: While chondrosarcoma can also present with a large mass and bone destruction, the presence of a discharging ulcer and significant bone erosion leans more towards osteosarcoma.

rejected.label: Ewing's Sarcoma
rejected.why: Ewing's sarcoma typically affects younger patients and often presents with systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss, which are not prominent in this case.

rejected.label: Soft Tissue Sarcoma
rejected.why: The primary involvement of the tibia bone and the radiographic appearance of bone erosion and destruction make soft tissue sarcoma less likely.

rejected.label: Dedifferentiated Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis would typically require histopathological confirmation, and the clinical presentation does not specifically suggest dedifferentiation from a pre-existing chondrosarcoma.
